title: Morning Robotics Scan
report:
## Waymo robotaxis attacked

### The Breakthrough
In Denver, a person repeatedly blocked Waymo driverless taxis with orange traffic cones and then threw eggs at them, forcing each vehicle to stop for cleaning and costing about $2,000 per incident. The attacks exploit Waymo Driver’s rule that treats traffic cones as non‑passable obstacles, causing the robotaxi to halt when boxed in, while egg‑throwing keeps it stationary for manual removal. This highlights a concrete safety vulnerability in a deployed autonomous vehicle system that directly impacts operational uptime.

### The Caveats
The claim rests only on isolated incident reports with no systematic testing or comparison to other autonomous fleets, leaving its broader significance unproven.

## MERLoc localization

### The Breakthrough
MERLoc turns a single 3‑D Gaussian‑splatting scan into a dense functional reference memory, enabling pose‑based retrieval that tolerates moving people and rearranged objects. By pre‑rendering reference views offline, the system runs on a Jetson Orin NX at 5 Hz and reduces position RMSE by 15‑60 % across nine of ten backend/split combinations compared to appearance‑based retrieval, demonstrating real‑world robustness in dynamic indoor hallways.

### The Caveats
The reported RMSE reductions are not anchored to any named baseline methods, making it unclear whether MERLoc truly outperforms established localization approaches.

## DexLink manipulation

### The Breakthrough
DexLink builds dexterous manipulation policies by chaining reusable hand‑object interaction templates, retargeting them to new objects and refining with residual reinforcement learning. This yields zero‑shot sim‑to‑real transfer without object‑specific demonstrations, matching dense reference‑tracking baselines in performance for both single‑hand and bimanual tasks.

### The Caveats
The claimed zero‑shot sim‑to‑real transfer is supported only by a qualitative demo, with no quantitative hardware benchmark or systematic real‑world evaluation.

## OneOcean marine benchmark

### The Breakthrough
OneOcean integrates real‑world bathymetry, currents, tides, and optional pollution data into a unified simulation suite that supports 2‑10 robots with 3‑6 DoF across dozens of navigation, station‑keeping, multi‑agent coordination, and cleanup tasks. The platform evaluates heuristic baselines, behavior cloning, and an LLM‑based planner, providing systematic stress‑testing of marine robot planners under varied dataset‑driven disturbances.

### The Caveats
The study reports results only in simulation, so it remains unproven whether the benchmark’s claimed benefits and planner performance transfer to real‑world marine robots.

## visloc-rs Rust SLAM

### The Breakthrough
visloc‑rs is a pure‑Rust library that implements SfM, visual‑inertial SLAM, multi‑session mapping and 3‑D Gaussian splatting, running GPU code via wgpu without C++/CUDA dependencies. Benchmarks show 3.46× faster ETH3D SfM than COLMAP with 25 % lower camera‑centre error and real‑time VIO on every EuRoC sequence (1.06‑1.68× speed), while also generating Gaussian‑splat scenes from thousands of images.

### The Caveats
The reported speed and accuracy gains are demonstrated only on a desktop GPU with offline datasets, without any closed‑loop robot or embedded‑hardware validation, so it’s unclear whether the Rust pipeline will deliver the same performance in real‑world robotic deployments.

## Real2SimLab benchmark platform

### The Breakthrough
Real2SimLab provides a unified open‑source platform that wraps existing benchmark scorers, allowing any of 47 supported coding agents or 5 non‑agent methods to be evaluated uniformly on six real‑to‑simulation benchmarks, with a data pipeline that filters out video‑recording contamination.

### The Caveats
The platform is not benchmarked against any existing real‑to‑simulation evaluation suites, so its claimed universality and advantages remain unvalidated.

## Evalkit agent evaluation

### The Breakthrough
Evalkit automates end‑to‑end evaluation, regression detection, and improvement loops for LLM‑driven agents by clustering execution traces into issue buckets and applying English‑rubric expert reviews, leading to a reported 90 % drop in failures, 80 % lower token consumption, and 45 % faster resolution in internal tests.

### The Caveats
The reported 90 % failure drop and token savings come only from internal tests with no external benchmark or comparison to existing agent‑evaluation tools, so its effectiveness outside the authors’ own setup is unproven.

## AV control beginners guide

### The Breakthrough
The repository bundles a step‑by‑step open textbook with Python simulations covering the full autonomous‑driving stack—localization, mapping, planning, and control—allowing users to run each algorithm with a single command and swap components within a documented software architecture.

### The Caveats
The repository provides only visual demos with no quantitative benchmarks or baseline comparisons, so its claimed educational value isn’t empirically validated.

### What to watch
Simulation and benchmarking tools are proliferating: OneOcean and Real2SimLab target domain‑specific (marine) and general real‑to‑simulation evaluation respectively, while visloc‑rs offers a Rust‑based SLAM pipeline that rivals traditional C++ stacks. Together they signal a push toward standardized, language‑agnostic evaluation frameworks, but each remains untested in closed‑loop robot deployments.

### Priority
The Waymo robotaxi safety incidents expose a tangible, real‑world vulnerability in deployed autonomous vehicles, making it the most urgent story for anyone building or studying embodied AI systems.

### One action
Monitor Waymo’s upcoming safety advisories and consider adding explicit cone‑detection and obstacle‑handling logic to your autonomous stack.
